stem: The Guru Granth Sahib keeps a hymn by Bhagat Dhanna in Raag Dhanasri (Ang 695) that asks God plainly for lentils, flour, ghee, shoes and a milk cow. What does Sikh tradition remember Dhanna as by trade?
options: a farmer who worked his own fields
a weaver who worked at a handloom
a barber who served at a king's court
a cobbler who worked with leather
why: Bhagat Dhanna is remembered as a Jat farmer from Rajasthan; his Dhanasri hymn on Ang 695 asks the Sustainer for a working household's needs. Kabir was a weaver, Sain a barber and Ravidas a leatherworker.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Dhanasri, Ang 695 (Bhagat Dhanna)

es.stem: El Guru Granth Sahib guarda un himno de Bhagat Dhanna en Raag Dhanasri (Ang 695) que le pide a Dios, sin rodeos, lentejas, harina, ghee, zapatos y una vaca lechera. ¿Qué oficio le atribuye la tradición sij a Dhanna?
options: un campesino que trabajaba sus tierras
un tejedor que trabajaba en un telar
un barbero que servía en la corte de un rey
un zapatero que trabajaba el cuero
es.why: La tradición recuerda a Bhagat Dhanna como un campesino jat de Rajastán; su himno en Dhanasri, en el Ang 695, le pide al Sustentador lo que necesita un hogar trabajador. Kabir era tejedor, Sain barbero y Ravidas trabajaba el cuero.

stem: Near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib (from Ang 1389), the Bhatts' swayye praise the Gurus one after another, and Bhatt Mathura describes the light passing from Guru Nanak to Angad, Amar Das, Ram Das and Arjan. What teaching do these verses express?
options: each Guru founded a separate school with its own teaching
the Gurus were kings to be praised for their wealth and rule
only Guru Nanak's own verses carry the light of the Guru
the Guru is one light, the same in each Guru who follows
why: The Bhatts' swayye (Ang 1389–1409) present the Guruship as one jot (light) passed on like a lamp lit from a lamp: different bodies, the same Guru.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Swayye of the Bhatts, Ang 1389–1409

es.stem: Cerca del final del Guru Granth Sahib (desde el Ang 1389), los swayye de los Bhatts alaban a los Gurús uno tras otro, y Bhatt Mathura describe la luz que pasa de Guru Nanak a Angad, Amar Das, Ram Das y Arjan. ¿Qué enseñanza expresan estos versos?
options: cada Gurú fundó una escuela distinta con su propia enseñanza
los Gurús eran reyes alabados por su riqueza y su poder
solo los versos de Guru Nanak llevan la luz del Gurú
el Gurú es una sola luz, la misma en cada Gurú que sigue
es.why: Los swayye de los Bhatts (Ang 1389–1409) presentan la Guruship como una sola jot (luz) que pasa como una lámpara encendida de otra lámpara: cuerpos distintos, el mismo Gurú.

stem: At Khidrana in 1705, the dying Mahan Singh asked Guru Gobind Singh to tear up the bedava, and the place became Muktsar. What was the bedava?
options: a treaty the Guru had made with the Mughal commanders
a list of Sikhs the Sirhind governor had ordered seized
a letter the Majha Sikhs had signed disowning the Guru
a hukamnama calling the Sikhs of Majha to Anandpur
why: During the siege of Anandpur, a band of Majha Sikhs left after signing a disclaimer (bedava) saying the Guru was not their Guru. Shamed and led back by Mai Bhago, they fought at Khidrana; the Guru tore up the paper and blessed them as the Forty Liberated Ones (Chali Mukte).
source: Sikh tradition of the Chali Mukte; Gurdwara Tuti Gandhi Sahib, Sri Muktsar Sahib

es.stem: En Khidrana, en 1705, Mahan Singh, moribundo, le pidió a Guru Gobind Singh que rompiera el bedava, y el lugar pasó a llamarse Muktsar. ¿Qué era el bedava?
options: un tratado que el Gurú había hecho con los jefes mogoles
una lista de sijs que el gobernador de Sirhind mandó apresar
una carta firmada por los sijs de Majha que renegaba del Gurú
un hukamnama que llamaba a los sijs de Majha a Anandpur
es.why: Durante el sitio de Anandpur, un grupo de sijs de Majha se fue tras firmar un documento (bedava) que decía que el Gurú no era su Gurú. Avergonzados y guiados de vuelta por Mai Bhago, lucharon en Khidrana; el Gurú rompió el papel y los bendijo como los Cuarenta Liberados (Chali Mukte).

stem: When Guru Gobind Singh sent Banda Singh Bahadur from Nanded to Punjab in 1708, tradition says he gave him five arrows from his quiver, along with five Sikhs, a drum, a banner and letters (hukamnamas). What did the arrows mainly signify?
options: the weapons he was to use in his first battle at Samana
that Banda was sent with the Guru's blessing and authority
that Banda had been named as the next Guru of the Sikh panth
payment for his years of service to the Guru at Nanded
why: The arrows, companions and hukamnamas told Punjab's Sikhs that this stranger came with the Guru's blessing and mandate. Tradition says the Guru also told him never to set himself up as Guru and to serve the Khalsa.
source: Sikh tradition of Banda Singh Bahadur's commission at Nanded, 1708

es.stem: Cuando Guru Gobind Singh envió a Banda Singh Bahadur de Nanded al Punyab en 1708, la tradición dice que le dio cinco flechas de su carcaj, junto con cinco sijs, un tambor, un estandarte y cartas (hukamnamas). ¿Qué significaban sobre todo las flechas?
options: las armas que debía usar en su primera batalla, en Samana
que Banda iba con la bendición y la autoridad del Gurú
que Banda había sido nombrado el siguiente Gurú de los sijs
el pago por sus años de servicio al Gurú en Nanded
es.why: Las flechas, los compañeros y los hukamnamas les decían a los sijs del Punyab que este desconocido venía con la bendición y el mandato del Gurú. La tradición dice que el Gurú también le pidió que nunca se presentara como Gurú y que sirviera al Khalsa.

stem: A landlord keeps most of the harvest that tenant farmers plowed, sowed and reaped. In the janamsakhi story of Guru Nanak at Saidpur, which food would that grain be most like?
options: the rich feast Malik Bhago held for holy men
the coarse bread Bhai Lalo the carpenter offered
the langar food Mata Khivi served at Khadur
the karah parshad shared at the close of a diwan
why: In the janamsakhi story, Guru Nanak squeezes Lalo's coarse bread and milk flows; from Malik Bhago's rich food comes blood, because it was taken from others' toil. It illustrates kirat karni, earning by honest work.
source: Janamsakhi tradition of Bhai Lalo and Malik Bhago

es.stem: Un terrateniente se queda con la mayor parte de la cosecha que los campesinos arrendatarios araron, sembraron y segaron. En el relato de los janamsakhis sobre Guru Nanak en Saidpur, ¿a qué comida se parecería más ese grano?
options: al rico banquete que Malik Bhago ofreció a los santos
al pan sencillo que ofreció Bhai Lalo, el carpintero
a la comida del langar que Mata Khivi servía en Khadur
al karah parshad que se reparte al cierre de un diwan
es.why: En el relato de los janamsakhis, Guru Nanak aprieta el pan sencillo de Lalo y brota leche; de la comida rica de Malik Bhago sale sangre, porque se tomó del esfuerzo de otros. Ilustra el kirat karni, ganarse la vida con trabajo honrado.

stem: Bhai Mani Singh had promised the Lahore governor a fee for letting Sikhs gather at Amritsar for Diwali, to be paid from the offerings. Why could he not pay it?
options: he spent the offerings on feeding the large crowds who came
he told Sikhs to stay away on hearing of a planned attack
the governor raised the fee once the gathering began
heavy rains kept the Sikhs from reaching Amritsar
why: Learning that the governor meant to send troops among the pilgrims, Bhai Mani Singh warned the Sikhs not to come; the offerings fell short, he was arrested, refused to give up his faith, and was executed in Lahore by being cut limb from limb. The Ardas remembers such martyrs.
source: Sikh tradition of Bhai Mani Singh's martyrdom, Lahore (1734 or 1738 in different accounts); the Ardas

es.stem: Bhai Mani Singh le había prometido al gobernador de Lahore una cuota por dejar que los sijs se reunieran en Amritsar para Diwali, que pagaría con las ofrendas. ¿Por qué no pudo pagarla?
options: gastó las ofrendas en dar de comer a la gente que vino
pidió a los sijs no ir al saber de un ataque planeado
el gobernador subió la cuota cuando empezó la reunión
unas lluvias fuertes impidieron a los sijs llegar a Amritsar
es.why: Al saber que el gobernador pensaba mandar tropas entre los peregrinos, Bhai Mani Singh avisó a los sijs que no fueran; las ofrendas no alcanzaron, lo arrestaron, se negó a dejar su fe y lo ejecutaron en Lahore cortándolo miembro por miembro. El Ardas recuerda a esos mártires.

stem: At the Sikh amrit ceremony, new members of the Khalsa are told who their spiritual father and mother are and where their home is. Who is named as their mother, and why is she remembered that way?
why: At amrit, initiates are told their father is Guru Gobind Singh, their mother Mata Sahib Kaur, and their home Anandpur Sahib. Tradition says she had no children of her own, and the Guru made her mother of the Khalsa.
source: Sikh Rehat Maryada, amrit sanskar; tradition of Mata Sahib Kaur

rubric.point: Names Mata Sahib Kaur as the Khalsa's mother. Naming Mata Gujri, Mata Sundari or 'the Guru's wife' without a name does not count.

Explains why: tradition says she had no children of her own and Guru Gobind Singh made her mother of the Khalsa, or that every initiate becomes her child, one family through amrit. 'Because she was the Guru's wife' alone counts as partly.
Mentions that Guru Gobind Singh is named as father and Anandpur (Sahib) as home, or that some tellings say she added sweets (patashe) to the first amrit (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En la ceremonia sij del amrit, a los nuevos miembros del Khalsa se les dice quiénes son su padre y su madre espirituales y cuál es su hogar. ¿A quién se nombra como su madre, y por qué se la recuerda así?
es.why: En el amrit, a los iniciados se les dice que su padre es Guru Gobind Singh, su madre Mata Sahib Kaur y su hogar Anandpur Sahib. La tradición dice que ella no tuvo hijos propios y que el Gurú la hizo madre del Khalsa.

stem: At Kup Rahira in February 1762, the day Sikhs call the Vadda Ghallughara (the great holocaust), Ahmad Shah Abdali's army caught a Sikh column of fighters traveling with their families. What did the fighters do, and why is the day remembered?
why: Rather than scatter, as horsemen could, the Khalsa fighters formed a ring around the families (the vahir) and fought while the column kept moving; very many Sikhs, fighters and families, were killed. The Ardas carries the memory of those who gave their lives.
source: Sikh tradition of the Vadda Ghallughara, 1762; Rattan Singh Bhangu, Prachin Panth Prakash

rubric.point: Says the fighters stayed with and shielded the families, for example by forming a ring around the column and fighting while it moved on, instead of scattering to save themselves. 'They fought bravely' without protecting the families counts as partly.
Says it is remembered for its enormous loss of Sikh lives, fighters and families together (the 'great holocaust'). Claiming the Sikhs won the battle does not count.

Mentions that the Khalsa is to protect the defenseless, that the dead are remembered in the Ardas, or that the Khalsa recovered within a few years, for example taking Sirhind in 1764 (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En Kup Rahira, en febrero de 1762, el día que los sijs llaman el Vadda Ghallughara (el gran holocausto), el ejército de Ahmad Shah Abdali alcanzó una columna sij de combatientes que viajaban con sus familias. ¿Qué hicieron los combatientes, y por qué se recuerda ese día?
es.why: En vez de dispersarse, como podían hacerlo los jinetes, los combatientes del Khalsa formaron un anillo alrededor de las familias (el vahir) y lucharon mientras la columna seguía avanzando; murieron muchísimos sijs, combatientes y familias. El Ardas guarda la memoria de quienes dieron la vida.
